title: Enterprise Dedicated: SLO-to-GPU Profile Triage & Intake Playbook
creator: Avery Chen
description: Deliver a runnable triage playbook and intake form that maps customer SLA targets (latency P95/P99, request QPS, sustained tokens/min) to recommended reserved throughput profiles and GPU class families. The playbook should be prescriptive enough for Solutions Eng to provide an initial reservation quote and for Eng to create sizing tickets with clear assumptions. This is non-bug product work focused on the enterprise intake flow for Dedicated capacity requests.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Intake form (Confluence + JSON schema) that collects: target latency (P95/P99), request distribution (sequence length histogram), steady QPS, peak QPS, burst allowance, routing regions, data residency, and failure budget requirements.
2) Triage rubric with scoring and a recommended throughput profile (e.g., Reserved-Standard, Reserved-High, Reserved-Burst) and GPU family suggestion (A100-40GB, H100-80GB, L4-class) and quantization knobs.
3) Example calculators (spreadsheet) for three customer archetypes demonstrating how scores map to a sample reservation and estimated monthly cost.
4) Decision matrix for autoscaling policy (static reservation, scheduled scale, reactive burst) and recommended default for each profile.
5) Hand-off checklist for Eng: model artifact requirements, perf test plan, KV cache expectations, guardrails for rollouts.
6) Playbook reviewed and approved by Solutions Eng, Runtime Eng, and Sales Engineering (approvals captured in comments).
decisions:
- Use a 0-100 triage score combining latency sensitivity (40%), steady throughput (25%), burst factor (15%), and compliance constraints (20%).
- Default GPU family recommendation: H100 for sustained long-context models where P95 < 250ms target at seq lengths > 2048; A100 for medium context and cost-sensitive; L4 for small-context embedding/semantic search workloads.
- Autoscaling tiers: Reserved-Standard -> allow 2x burst for 10 minutes; Reserved-High -> allow 3x burst up to 30 minutes; Enterprise-Burst -> schedule and reactive policies with pre-warmed pool.
- For customers with hard P99 SLAs and multi-region failover, require Dedicated cross-region fallback with pre-warmed replicas (documented in hand-off).
